battle.name: 布狄卡的起義
battle.theater: 英國東南部與米德蘭戰線
battle.brief: 公元60至61年春，布狄卡率伊西尼人起兵，先焚卡姆魯敦，再破倫敦與維魯拉米烏姆，末了在英格蘭中部與蘇埃托尼烏斯·保利諾斯的兩軍團加援軍決戰，義軍覆滅，女王服毒自盡。卡面這支埃及長矛是遠古青銅矛的樣式，落到一世紀的英格蘭戰場，已換成套接式鐵矛。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 布狄卡的起義是公元一世紀初羅馬不列顛行省內的一場大規模部落起義。英方聯盟以東安格利亞的伊西尼人為主，首領是女王布狄卡；同盟還有掌握卡姆魯敦的特里諾萬特人，其後米德蘭的卡圖維拉尼人、科爾尼人等部族相繼加入，起義的規模很快擴展到整個東南部與中部。英軍並非常備軍，沒有固定兵員與後勤體系，作戰單位是各部族按首領集結的戰士方陣，貴族與首領率領核心戰士，戰力建立在大量步兵、長矛與標槍、投石索手、騎兵與雙輪輕車之上，車上常帶削尖的鐮刀，用來衝撞羅馬陣線。羅馬方是行省的整套軍事機器：總督兼軍團長蓋烏斯·蘇埃托尼烏斯·保利諾斯坐鎮，率駐軍第II奧古斯塔、第IX希斯帕納等軍團，各式輔助步兵大隊與騎兵中隊，以及由艦隊分遣的海軍陸戰隊；行省總督府還有常駐不列顛的財政官艾利諾斯。城鎮方面，卡姆魯敦、倫敦、維魯拉米烏姆三座羅馬城市由退役老兵聚居，構成帝國在島上的統治骨幹。起義爆發後，尼祿從萊茵河調來佩蒂利烏斯·凱里亞利斯與第XIV軍團，又從西班牙召回第IX軍團，由尤利烏斯·阿格里科拉押送；布里干特人由附庸女王卡爾蒂曼杜統率，站在羅馬一方出騎兵平叛。兩造的差距不在單兵，而在組織：羅馬有軍團與後勤線，英軍有數量與士氣。
countriesEn: Boudica's revolt was a large tribal rising inside the Roman province of Britannia in the early first century AD. On the British side the alliance was led by the Iceni of East Anglia under its queen, Boudica; the Trinovantes, who held Camulodunum, joined her, and afterwards peoples of the Midlands such as the Catuvellauni and the Cornovii came in, so that the rising quickly spread across the whole south-east and centre of the island. The British host was no standing army: there were no fixed ranks, no standing roster and no logistics system, and the fighting unit was a levy mustered by each tribal chief. Nobles and war-lords led the core of the warband, and the strength of the force lay in mass infantry carrying long spears and javelins, slingers, cavalry and two-wheeled light chariots whose axle-blades were sharpened for the charge against a Roman shield-line. The Roman side was the whole military machinery of the province. Gaius Suetonius Paulinus, legate and commander of the legions, held overall command, with legio II Augusta and legio IX Hispana, a range of auxiliary infantry cohorts and cavalry alae, and detachments of marines from the fleet. The governor's administration also included the procurator of the province, Alpinus. Three Roman towns — Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium — were settled by veterans and formed the backbone of imperial government on the island. Once the revolt broke out Nero sent Petillius Cerialis with legio XIV Gemina from the Rhine, and recalled legio IX Hispana from Spain under Julius Agricola. The Brigantes, ruled by the client queen Cartimandua, took the Roman side and supplied the very cavalry the insurgents most conspicuously lacked. The gap between the two sides was not in the individual soldier but in organisation: Rome had legions and supply lines, the Britons had numbers and morale.
people: 布狄卡是起義的核心人物，古代史家的描述相當一致：塔西佗說她身材高大、力量充沛、衣著華麗，走到陣前時把斗篷撩到一邊，用粗壯的聲音發表講話；卡西烏斯·狄奧則稱她極有智慧，又極為勇猛，並記下她對部眾的宣言。實際上，起義的策劃與執行都出自她手：她整合伊西尼與特里諾萬特兩部的力量，決定先打英軍視為心臟的卡姆魯敦，分兵攻擊倫敦與維魯拉米烏姆，最後率全軍與羅馬援軍決戰。據記載她在戰車上率領女兒同行，隨身有長矛與短劍，殺至戰陣之中。最終之戰失敗後，據塔西佗與狄奧記載，她服毒自盡，不肯被押往羅馬受辱，屍身被部眾秘密掩埋，葬處從未被找到。羅馬方面的關鍵人物同樣集中：總督保利諾斯是老練的將領，曾在莫里塔尼亞與亞美尼亞打過仗，也在阿格里科拉之前鎮壓過蒙島，駐軍英格蘭後先取安格爾西島再修路直抵內陸，他起初判斷起義只是騷擾，據報聽到卡姆魯敦陷落時正在遠處，只帶騎兵兼程趕回，等於放棄了第一場會戰的時機。接手戰局的凱里亞利斯是第XIV軍團的軍團長，阿格里科拉當時是保民官級的指揮官，兩人自萊茵河與西班牙調兵入英；財政官艾利諾斯在卡姆魯敦陣亡。附庸女王卡爾蒂曼杜的選擇則改變了戰局走向：布里干特人站在羅馬一方，叛軍最缺的就是騎兵。
peopleEn: Boudica is the central figure of the rising, and the ancient historians describe her consistently. Tacitus says she was tall and strong, dressed in fine clothes, and that when she came before the army she threw back her cloak and spoke in a deep, resonant voice; Cassius Dio calls her a woman of great intelligence and also a very brave one, and records the speech she made to her people. In practice both the planning and the execution of the revolt were hers: she welded the Iceni and the Trinovantes together, chose Camulodunum — the place the Romans themselves regarded as the heart of the province — as the first target, split her forces to strike Londinium and Verulamium, and led the whole host into the decisive engagement with the Roman reinforcements. She is said to have ridden into battle in her chariot with her daughters beside her, armed with a long spear and a short sword, and to have fought at the front line. When the final battle was lost, Tacitus and Dio both record that she took poison rather than be led in Roman triumph, and that her people buried her in secret, so that her grave has never been found. The decisive figures on the Roman side are equally concentrated. The governor Paulinus was an experienced commander who had campaigned in Mauretania and Armenia and had already crushed the Monae before Agricola, taking the island of Anglesey and driving a road deep into the interior; he judged the rising at first to be little more than a raid, and by the report of the fall of Camulodunum he was some distance away and rode up with the cavalry, which cost him the chance of meeting the rebels in force. Cerialis, who took over, was the legate of legio XIV Gemina, and Agricola at that moment was a commander of praetorian rank escorting the Ninth from Spain. The procurator Alpinus was killed at Camulodunum. The choice of the client queen Cartimandua also shaped the outcome: the Brigantes stood with Rome, and cavalry was exactly what the rebels lacked.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛是早王朝時期的樣式：銅或青銅矛頭以綁紮方式固定在木杆上，是人類最早成形的直刺兵器之一，埃及人用它守城垣，也用它收復失地。它的戰術位置很單純——正兵相接時的第一擊與第二擊，必須比短劍快、比重斧長，並且能用木杆承受衝撞。一世紀的英格蘭戰場上，同類的直刺兵器已經換了材質：伊西尼人與卡圖維拉尼人使用的長矛是套接式鐵矛，矛頭以套筒固定於木杆，全長接近兩米，配合大尺寸木盾（外覆獸皮或金屬飾片）組成密集矛牆，後排再以標槍與投石索手覆蓋。與之相對的羅馬步兵是重裝行列：執大盾與短劍，以重投槍先手軟化對手，接著貼身穿甲兵破陣；卡姆魯敦出土的裝備殘件說明帝國邊軍的鎧甲有鎖子甲與分段甲兩種工藝。布狄卡的車隊是另一件關鍵裝備：雙輪輕車加削尖前鐮，衝入羅馬陣線時可直接切斷前列盾牌與人腿；蘇埃托尼烏斯記載起義軍還帶著一具自卡姆魯敦繳獲的羅馬弩炮，用來壓制羅馬步兵線。交通方面，英軍靠部族領地就地取糧與隨軍輜重車補給，羅馬方面靠泰晤士河船隊與軍用帳篷車隊維持戰役節奏，兩軍的補給距離與速度，決定了各自能撐多久的圍攻與追擊。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is an early dynastic Egyptian spear: a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by binding, one of the earliest straight-thrust weapons ever made in regular form, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and to win back lost ground. Its tactical place is simple and it never changes: the first and second stroke of close combat, delivered faster than a sword, longer than an axe, and borne on a shaft that can absorb the shock. On the battlefields of England in the first century the same family of thrusting weapon had simply changed material. The Iceni and the Catuvellauni carried socketed iron spearheads, the head fitted into a socket at the butt of a wooden shaft, giving a weapon close to two metres long, and they formed dense spear-walls behind large wooden shields covered with hide or metal plates, with javelin-men and slingers ranged behind them. The Roman infantry opposite them was a close-order arm: scutum and gladius, softened by the pilum thrown at range, followed by armoured swordsmen who broke the enemy line at contact. The equipment recovered at Camulodunum shows that the empire's frontier troops were supplied with both chain mail and segmented plate. Boudica's chariots were the other key piece of equipment: a two-wheeled car with a sharpened blade on the axle, which could cut into a Roman shield-line and take legs with it as it charged. Suetonius records that the rebel army also brought a Roman ballista captured at Camulodunum, used to press the Roman infantry line. In terms of transport, the British drew grain in the tribal territory they held and carried it on baggage waggons, while Rome worked on the Thames shipping and its tent-waggon train; the distance and the speed of each side's supply determined how long either could sustain a siege or a pursuit.
tactics: 英軍的戰術以奇襲與分割著稱。卡姆魯敦是行省首府，城牆未完工、防備最薄，起義軍趁羅馬主力分散、主力在外圍巡邏之際，以伊西尼與特里諾萬特戰士猛撲城門與城牆缺口；城中老兵與輔助軍倉促應戰，帝國祭壇與城市隨之被焚。得手之後，英軍分兵：一部直撲倫敦，另一部取維魯拉米烏姆，迫使羅馬總督在兩線之間疲於奔命；倫敦一線因防守兵力單薄，商人與居民未及撤離，城內商館與住宅盡付一炬，維魯拉米烏姆亦遭掠奪。英軍的正面戰法是車騎在前、步兵結成人字形矛陣向前推，喊聲震天，矛牆齊推，以長矛的長度吃過羅馬重裝步兵的短兵；投射武器方面以標槍與投石索壓制羅馬陣線，一旦近身，即以短劍與矛柄纏鬥。羅馬方面的應對有兩層：一是保利諾斯放棄城鎮退守野外部隊，二是情報與行軍速度——英軍斥候把羅馬援軍接近的消息傳回，起義軍遂在援軍抵達前傾巢出戰。最終之戰中，保利諾斯把兩支主力軍團置於中央，輔助步兵大隊分列兩翼，騎兵中隊在兩翼外側，輜重與傷員在後方營地，選地平坦而可退入營壘；英軍以巨大車陣與密集步兵直撞中央，羅馬中央一度被突破，兩翼遭包圍，軍團退成楔形，結盾抵禦退回營地。營地設在可守的地形上，英軍圍攻數日不能下，聞知凱里亞利斯主力已近，遂解散退回部族。
tacticsEn: The British way of fighting turned on surprise and division. Camulodunum was the capital of the province, its defences unfinished and its garrison thinnest, and the insurgents struck while the Roman field force was dispersed and the garrison was out on patrol: Iceni and Trinovantes warriors hit the gates and the gaps in the wall, the veterans and auxiliaries inside answered in disorder, and the imperial cult temple and the town itself went up in flame. Having won, the British split their force. One part went straight for Londinium, another for Verulamium, and the Roman governor was forced to shuttle between two fronts. The London line was defended by too few troops for the traders and inhabitants to get clear, so the commercial quarter and the houses burned; Verulamium was sacked as well. The British method of decision was to put chariots and cavalry in front, the infantry in a wedge or boar's-head formation pressing forward, the whole host shouting as it came on, the spear-walls advancing together so that the British spear was longer than the Roman's short weapon, with javelins and sling-stones thrown at the Roman line before contact was made, and then, once close, fighting with short swords and with the shafts themselves. Rome's answer had two layers. Paulinus abandoned the towns and fell back on a field army; and he used intelligence and marching speed, for British scouts carried the news of the approaching relief force back to the rebels, and they moved out to meet the enemy before the reinforcements could arrive. In the final battle Paulinus put the two legions in the centre, the auxiliary cohorts on the wings, the cavalry alae beyond them, and the baggage and wounded behind the camp, on ground that was level and gave access to his own enclosure. The British drove their chariots and massed infantry straight at the centre and broke it; the wings were surrounded, the legions drew back in a wedge, closed shields and made for the camp. The camp stood on defensible ground and the British could not take it after several days of assault; on learning that Cerialis was close they dispersed back to their tribes.
data: 古代記載的數字彼此出入很大，只能當作量級參考。塔西佗記卡姆魯敦一役羅馬方面陣亡約一萬五千人（含城內老兵與居民），蘇埃托尼烏斯則記為二萬兵員；全戰役的死亡人數，兩家都說到數萬以上，塔西佗給出的戰役總死亡數是約七萬人，奧羅西烏斯最為誇張，寫成羅馬方面死八萬、英方死二十萬。兵員方面，一世紀中期一個軍團的戰鬥兵力約五千至五千五百人，兩支主力軍團加三個營的輔助步兵大隊（巴達維亞與通格里亞人為主）與多個騎兵中隊，羅馬救援總兵力在兩萬上下；英軍方面沒有可核的數字，古代作家形容為前所未見的大軍，現代估計從數萬到十萬不等，比較保守的算法是五至六萬名能戰之士，車隊數目亦被記為極大。距離與時間上，倫敦到維魯拉米烏姆約三十三公里，保利諾斯在倫敦以北約五十公里處聞警，救援軍自萊茵河調動、渡海、接戰，前後耗時數月；從起事到平定約四個月，歷經春夏。地名的關鍵一處是英格蘭中部的主戰場，其位置至今有沿沃特林街一線、曼徹斯特郡一帶等數種說法，沒有定論。考古方面，卡姆魯敦的燃燒層與三座城市的錢幣窖藏，佐證了起義的規模：霍克森窖藏約一萬五千枚金幣、兩萬三千餘枚銀幣與一千枚青銅幣，埋藏時間正落在此亂世。
dataEn: The figures in the ancient sources differ sharply and can only be used as orders of magnitude. Tacitus gives about fifteen thousand Roman dead at Camulodunum, counting the veterans and civilians of the town, while Suetonius puts it at twenty thousand soldiers; for the rising as a whole both speak of tens of thousands, Tacitus giving a total of about seventy thousand dead, and Orosius being the most extravagant of all with eighty thousand Romans and two hundred thousand Britons. On numbers of troops: a mid-first-century legion carried roughly five to five and a half thousand men, so two legions, with three auxiliary infantry cohorts — mostly Batavian and Tungrian — and a number of cavalry alae, put the Roman relief force at around twenty thousand. For the British there is no checkable figure; ancient writers speak of an army greater than any Rome had seen in Britain, and modern estimates run from tens of thousands to a hundred thousand, with a conservative figure of fifty to sixty thousand fighting men, and the number of chariots likewise described as very great. On distance and time: Londinium to Verulamium is about thirty-three kilometres, Paulinus was some fifty kilometres north of London when the alarm reached him, and the relief force had to be moved from the Rhine, cross the sea and come to grips, which took months; from the outbreak to the pacification about four months passed, running through spring and summer. The one place that matters in the topography is the battlefield in the English Midlands, whose site remains disputed, with proposals including a line along Watling Street and ground in the Mancetter area; there is no settled answer. The archaeology gives the scale of the rising: the burning layer at Camulodunum, and coin hoards in the affected towns. The Hoxne hoard alone holds about fifteen thousand gold coins, more than twenty-three thousand silver and a thousand bronze, and it was buried in precisely this disorder.
cause: 起義的直接導火線，是伊西尼國王普拉蘇塔古斯死後羅馬官員對其遺產的處理。普拉蘇塔古斯無子嗣，臨終把國土立遺囑留給女兒們，同時交給尼祿皇帝，企圖以象徵性的讓渡換取王國被兼併時的優惠；羅馬的財政官與地方官員卻把這份讓渡當成全面吞併的依據，島上已沒有一個可以正式申辯的本地君主。卡西烏斯·狄奧記載，兩名女兒被押作人質，女王在宮中受辱，其中甚至有鞭打與凌辱的情節；地方上原有的伊西尼人武力被解散，部落的青壯被徵發或被要求交出武器，交納的貢賦與糧食又年年加緊。三年的怨恨之所以在一年之內爆發，正因為矛盾是疊加上去的：早年圖拉真曾允許部落王保留土地與武力，尼祿時期的總督政策則把羅馬式的地籍、直接稅與老兵安置同時壓到部族身上。更深一層，羅馬在卡姆魯敦修建的帝國崇拜中心與大批殖民者，本身就是對部落主權的挑釁，考古挖出的被斬首的皇帝像殘件，說明起義軍攻入城中後，矛頭直指帝國崇拜的象徵。於是，奪回被沒收的王室產業、恢復部落自治、趕走城中的羅馬人與拉丁化商人，成為起義公開的目標；英軍攻陷三城的順序，也正是這種象徵性打擊的邏輯。
causeEn: The immediate trigger of the revolt was the way Roman officials handled the estate of Prasutagus, king of the Iceni, after his death. Prasutagus had no son, and on his deathbed he left the kingdom to his daughters together with the emperor Nero, hoping that a symbolic cession would buy favourable terms when the kingdom was absorbed. The Roman procurators and the local officials treated that cession as the legal pretext for outright annexation, and there was no longer any native ruler with standing to argue the case. Cassius Dio records that the two daughters were taken as hostages, that the queen was ill-treated in her own court, with flogging and worse, and that the armed body of the Iceni was disbanded, young men were conscripted or required to surrender their weapons, and tribute and grain were demanded more heavily with every year. The accumulated resentment of three years broke out inside a single year precisely because the injuries were layered: early in the century Trajan had allowed tribal kings to keep their lands and their armed followers, whereas the policy of Nero's governors applied Roman land registration, direct taxation and the settlement of veterans to the tribes at the same time. Deeper still, the imperial cult centre Rome built at Camulodunum, and the great population of Roman settlers inside it, were themselves a challenge to tribal sovereignty; the headless imperial statues the excavators recovered show that when the rebels entered the town their target was the visible emblem of the imperial cult. Recovering the confiscated royal property, restoring tribal autonomy and driving out the Romans and the Latinised traders in the towns thus became the declared object of the rising, and the order in which the three towns were taken follows exactly that logic of symbolic strike.
impact: 起義的直接後果，是羅馬在英國的統治成本被徹底重估。三座羅馬城市被毀：卡姆魯敦在起義後的重建中整體放棄了原有的城市格局，倫敦的商業街區盡毀，直到二十世紀後期考古才確認其下有厚達一公尺以上的燃燒堆積層，維魯拉米烏姆同樣受創。帝國在島上的城市網絡與財政循環——尤其倫敦那些以信用交易維生的商人的資本——幾乎一次清零，羅馬政府此後對不列顛的財政撥款明顯增加。戰略上，羅馬放棄了王國臣附的治理模式：布里干特人的附庸王國同樣被解散，附庸女王卡爾蒂曼杜被迫逃往羅馬一側，島上再無保留的本地王權。隨後的軍事部署也因起義而改變：第IX希斯帕納軍團北調，第XX瓦萊里亞軍團於公元六十六年入英駐防，英格蘭北部與西部的征服被提上日程，斯坦尼蓋特與後來的哈德良長城，都是這條路線上的下一站。長期而言，起義摧毀了羅馬化不列顛的都市與行政骨架，公元五世紀羅曼治權在島上崩解時，這座城市網的斷裂常被學者視為其中一環；而布狄卡本人作為不列顛反羅馬抵抗的象徵，在十九世紀以後被不斷重述，1902年豎立於威斯敏斯特橋端的青銅像，就是這條形象線的定點。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the revolt was a complete reappraisal of what it cost Rome to hold Britain. The three Roman towns were destroyed. Camulodunum, rebuilt after the rising, abandoned its former urban plan; the commercial quarter of Londinium was burned to the ground, and it was only late twentieth-century archaeology that confirmed a burning deposit more than a metre thick beneath the modern city; Verulamium was gutted as well. The network of towns and the fiscal circulation of the province — above all the merchant capital of London, which ran on credit transactions — were wiped out in a single stroke, and Roman financial allocations to Britannia rose noticeably afterwards. Strategically, Rome abandoned the model of a client kingdom: the client kingdom of the Brigantes was dissolved as well, the client queen Cartimandua was driven to the Roman side, and no native kingship survived on the island. The garrison pattern changed too: legio IX Hispana was moved north, and legio XX Valeria Victrix was brought to Britain in AD 66, so that the conquest of the north and west of the island moved up the agenda, with the Stanegate and later Hadrian's Wall as the next stages of the same road. In the long run the rising destroyed the urban and administrative skeleton of Romanised Britain, and when Roman government in the island collapsed in the fifth century the fracture of that town network is often counted by scholars as one of its elements. Boudica herself, as the emblem of British resistance to Rome, was retold again and again after the nineteenth century, and the bronze statue set up at the western end of Westminster Bridge in 1902 is the fixed point of that line of imagery.
result: 結果是羅馬的慘勝。最終一戰，義軍的攻勢被羅馬中央縱隊頂住，兩翼被切斷，車隊與步兵在退回營地時被大量殺傷，營地又被英軍圍攻數日而不能下；英軍得知第XIV軍團已近，失去了再攻的時間，遂解散退回各自的部族。布狄卡本人沒有被俘，據塔西佗與狄奧記載，她服毒而死，部眾將她秘密安葬，從此下落不明。起義隊伍隨之瓦解：伊西尼與特里諾萬特繳械，被要求交出武器並提供人質；米德蘭各部族另行鎮壓，殘餘武裝被清剿。羅馬方面，總督保利諾斯雖然守住了行省，卻因判斷失誤、屢失城邑被召回，接任者佩特羅尼烏斯·圖爾皮利安努斯於公元六十六年抵任，第一次以總督兼軍團長的體制重整行省，並把治理重點轉向北方與財政整頓。蘇埃托尼烏斯記載，繳獲的武器被運回羅馬陳列，數量之大，讓羅馬的凱旋看來比實際戰果更為盛大——這正好說明這場戰爭的真實代價：帝國保住了行省，卻花上了三座城市的血肉。
resultEn: The result was a costly Roman victory. In the last engagement the British attack was checked by the Roman centre, the wings were cut off, and the chariots and infantry were cut down in the withdrawal towards the camp, which the British then assaulted for several days without success; learning that the Fourteenth Legion was close, they lost the time for another assault and dispersed back to their own tribes. Boudica was not taken alive. Tacitus and Dio both say that she took poison, and her people buried her in secret, after which her resting place was never found. The rebel host dissolved with her: the Iceni and the Trinovantes gave up their weapons and were made to surrender hostages; the Midlands peoples were suppressed separately and the remaining armed bands were hunted down. On the Roman side the governor Paulinus saved the province but was recalled after misjudging the rising and losing town after town, and his successor Petronius Turpilianus arrived in AD 66 to reorganise the province for the first time under a single legate who combined governorship with the command of the legions, shifting the focus of government towards the north and towards fiscal retrenchment. Suetonius records that the captured weapons were carried back to Rome for display, and that their sheer number made the Roman triumph look greater than the victory actually was — which is precisely the true cost of this war: the empire kept the province, and paid for it with the blood of three cities.
